newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean women petition for cheaper condoms.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean women petition for cheaper condoms.

text.p: At least 20,000 Zimbabweans have petitioned President Robert Mugabe's government to ensure female condoms become more accessible and affordable to ordinary women to help cut the spread of the deadly AIDS disease.
The petition was initiated by Zimbabwe's Women and AIDS Support Network.
Its co-ordinator, Priscilla Misihairambwi, said on Monday that the female condom sold at 20 Zimbabwe dollars ($2.00) was too expensive for many women.
Urging the government to subsidise the price, Misihairambwi told reporters: "We want a situation where women have equal access to the Femidom as men have to the condom."
Male condoms are handed out free at health clinics, but woman have complained that men are reluctant to use protection.
Figures from the Ministry of Health show an estimated 10 percent of Zimbabwe's 10.5 million population is infected with the HIV virus that leads to AIDS, the majority of whom are women and children.
